spots.name: Mauritshuis
spots.summary: The Mauritshuis is an art museum in The Hague, Netherlands. The museum houses the Royal Cabinet of Paintings which consists of 854 objects, mostly Dutch Golden Age paintings.

names.ja: マウリッツハイス美術館

spots.name: Binnenhof
spots.summary: The Binnenhof is a complex of buildings in the city centre of The Hague, Netherlands, next to the Hofvijver. It houses the meeting place of both houses of the States General of the Netherlands, as well as the Ministry of General Affairs and the office of the prime minister of the Netherlands.

spots.name: Huis ten Bosch

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Huis ten Bosch is a royal palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It is one of three official residences of the Dutch monarch; the two others being the Noordeinde Palace in The Hague and the Royal Palace of Amsterdam.

spots.name: Madurodam
spots.summary: Madurodam is a miniature park and tourist attraction in the Scheveningen district of The Hague in the Netherlands. It is home to a range of 1:25 scale model replicas of famous Dutch landmarks, historical cities and large developments.

spots.name: Noordeinde Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Noordeinde Palace is one of three official palaces of the Dutch royal family. Located in the city centre of The Hague in the province of South Holland, it has been used as the official workplace of King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima since 2013.

spots.name: Scheveningen
spots.summary: Scheveningen is one of the eight districts of The Hague, Netherlands, as well as a subdistrict of that city. Scheveningen is a modern seaside resort with a long, sandy beach, an esplanade, a pier, and a lighthouse. The beach is popular for water sports such as windsurfing and kiteboarding.

spots.name: Peace Palace
spots.summary: The Peace Palace is an international courthouse in The Hague, Netherlands. It houses the International Court of Justice, and the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA).

photo.author: International Court of Justice; originally uploaded by Yeu Ninje at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Grote or Sint-Jacobskerk

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Great Church or St. James's Church is a landmark Reformed Protestant church in The Hague, Netherlands. The building is located on the Torenstraat, named for its high tower. Together with the Binnenhof, it is one of the oldest buildings in The Hague.

spots.name: Den Haag HS railway station
spots.summary: Den Haag HS, an abbreviation of the original name Den Haag Hollands Spoor, is the oldest train station in The Hague, South Holland, Netherlands, located on the Amsterdam–Haarlem–Rotterdam railway. It is the second main station in The Hague and, unlike The Hague Central Station, it is not a terminus station.

names.it: Stazione di Den Haag Hollands Spoor

spots.name: Ridderzaal
spots.summary: The Ridderzaal is the main building of the 13th-century inner square of the former castle of the counts of Holland called Binnenhof at the address Binnenhof 11 in The Hague, Netherlands.

spots.name: Kunstmuseum Den Haag

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Kunstmuseum Den Haag is an art museum in The Hague in the Netherlands, founded in 1866 as the Museum voor Moderne Kunst. Later, until 1998, it was known as Haags Gemeentemuseum, and until the end of September 2019 as Gemeentemuseum Den Haag.

spots.name: Torentje

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torentje, located at the Binnenhof in The Hague next to the Mauritshuis museum, has been the office of the Prime Minister of the Netherlands since 1982.

spots.name: Kneuterdijk Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kneuterdijk Palace is a former royal palace of the Netherlands located in The Hague, nowadays the seat of the Council of State. Built in 1716 in the Louis XIV style by architect Daniel Marot, it was commissioned by Count Johan Hendrik of Wassenaer-Obdam, member of the House of Wassenaer.

spots.name: Gevangenpoort

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Gevangenpoort is a former gate and medieval prison on the Buitenhof in The Hague, Netherlands. It is situated next to the 18th-century art gallery founded by William V, Prince of Orange in 1774 known as the Prince William V Gallery.

spots.name: Het Strijkijzer
spots.summary: Het Strijkijzer is a residential and office skyscraper in The Hague, Netherlands. It is 132 metres (433 ft) with 43 floors, making it the city's fourth tallest building.

spots.name: Plein
spots.summary: Plein or het Plein is a town square in the old city centre of The Hague in the Netherlands.

spots.name: Hofvijver
spots.summary: The Hofvijver is a small lake in the centre of The Hague, Netherlands. its water volume approximately is 32000 m³ It is adjoined in the east by the Korte Vijverberg road, in the south by the Binnenhof and the Mauritshuis, in the west by the Buitenhof and in the north by the Lange Vijverberg road.

spots.name: KB, nationale bibliotheek

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The KB National Library of the Netherlands is the national library of the Netherlands, based in The Hague, founded in 1798.

spots.name: Malieveld
spots.summary: Malieveld is a large grass field in the city center of The Hague, Netherlands, located opposite the central train station. The field is widely known in the Netherlands for being the location of many large-scale demonstrations. It is also used for festivals, funfairs, concerts and other big events.

spots.name: Escher Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Escher in Het Paleis is a museum in The Hague, Netherlands, featuring the works of the Dutch graphical artist M. C. Escher. It is housed in the Lange Voorhout Palace since November 2002.

spots.name: Louwman Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Louwman Museum is a museum for historic cars, coaches, and motorcycles in The Hague, Netherlands. It has been situated on the Leidsestraatweg near the A44 motorway since 2010. The museum's former names are "Nationaal Automobiel Museum" and "Louwman Collection".

spots.name: Nieuwe Kerk

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nieuwe Kerk is a Dutch Baroque Protestant church in The Hague, located across from the modern city hall on the Spui. It was built in 1649 after the Great Church had become too small. Construction was completed in 1656.

spots.name: Hoftoren

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hoftoren, nicknamed De Vulpen, is a 29-storey, 141.86-metre-high (465.4 ft) building in The Hague, Netherlands. It is the third-tallest building in the city, and the eighth-tallest in the country.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Jensbn~commonswiki assumed (based on copyri

spots.name: Buitenhof
spots.summary: The Buitenhof is a square in The Hague, Netherlands, adjacent to the Binnenhof and the Hofvijver. It is listed in the Top 100 Dutch heritage sites.

spots.name: Lange Voorhout Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lange Voorhout Palace in The Hague was designed in 1760 by the architect Pieter de Swart for Anthony Patras (1718-1764), a deputy to the States General of the Netherlands.

names.ja: ランゲ・フォールハウト宮殿

spots.name: Old City Hall
spots.summary: The Old City Hall in The Hague is a Renaissance-style building on the Groenmarkt near the Grote Kerk. It is the former seat of the city's government, and remains a place where residents hold civic wedding ceremonies, and where the royal family register their family births.

names.fr: Ancien hôtel de ville de La Haye

spots.name: Lange Voorhout
spots.summary: The Lange Voorhout is a street in the old city centre of The Hague, Netherlands. This L-shaped street runs from Kneuterdijk in the west to Toernooiveld in the east, reaching approximately 0.47 kilometres (0.29 mi) in length.

spots.name: Kloosterkerk

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kloosterkerk is a church on the Lange Voorhout in The Hague, Netherlands. The church and its accompanying monastery were first built in 1397. The church is known today as the church where Beatrix of the Netherlands occasionally attended services.

spots.name: Prince William V Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Prince William V Gallery is an art gallery on the Buitenhof in The Hague that currently shares an entrance with the Gevangenpoort museum. It is a recreation of the original gallery Galerij Prins Willem V, once founded there by William V, Prince of Orange, in 1774.

names.ja: 皇太子ウィリアム5世のギャラリー

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

names.nl: Voormalige Ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken: Ministerie van Waterstaat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Royal Academy of Art
spots.summary: The Royal Academy of Art is an art and design academy in The Hague, offering programs at both the HBO bachelor's and master's levels, as well as PhD programs.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Royal Academy of Art, The Hague

names.fr: Académie royale des beaux-arts de La Haye
names.es: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de La Haya

spots.name: Museum Bredius

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Museum Bredius is a museum showing the collection of the early twentieth century Dutch art historian Abraham Bredius.

spots.name: Indies Monument
spots.summary: The Indies Monument is a memorial in The Hague in memory of all Dutch citizens and soldiers killed during World War II as a result of the Japanese occupation (1942–1945) of the former Dutch East Indies. It is dedicated to all who died in battle, in prison camps or during forced labor.

spots.name: Beelden aan Zee

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Beelden aan Zee museum in the Scheveningen district of The Hague, founded in 1994 by the sculpture collectors Theo and Lida Scholten, is the only Dutch museum which specialises in only exhibiting sculpture.

names.ja: ベールデン・アン・ゼー

spots.name: Agnetapark
spots.summary: Agnetapark was an area of workers' housing in Delft, South Holland, the Netherlands. It was one of the highest quality workers' housing areas built before the Housing Act of 1902 was imposed. It was 'transformed' from a marshy 4 hectares area of land to a 'paradise' of industry.

spots.name: European Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The European Library was an Internet service that allows access to the resources of 49 European national libraries and an increasing number of research libraries. Searching is free and delivers metadata records as well as digital objects, mostly free of charge.

spots.name: Haags Historisch Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Haags Historisch Museum is a museum situated on the Korte Vijverberg in The Hague, Netherlands, dedicated to the history of the city. It is based in the one-time guild house of Saint Sebastian.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

photo.author: Roel Wijnants from The Hague, The Netherlands-Nederland

spots.name: Scheveningen Pier
spots.summary: The Scheveningen Pier is a pleasure pier in the Dutch resort town of Scheveningen near The Hague. Opened in 1961, the current pier is the second in the town, the first being lost just after, and as a result of, the Second World War.

spots.name: Museum Voorlinden
spots.summary: Museum Voorlinden is an art museum in Wassenaar in the Netherlands. It was founded and is privately owned by Joop van Caldenborgh. It was opened on 10 September 2016 by King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site
Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Pulchri Studio

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pulchri Studio is a Dutch art society, art institution and art studio based in The Hague ('s-Gravenhage), Netherlands.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Oranjehotel
spots.summary: The Hague Penitentiary Institution is a Dutch prison that is part of the Judicial Institutions Department of the Ministry of Justice. It can accommodate more than 1,000 detainees and consists of two locations, at Zoetermeer and Scheveningen.

spots.name: Royal Stables
spots.summary: The Royal Stables is a collection of equestrian stables of the Dutch royal family, the House of Orange-Nassau. It is a Rijksmonumental building that is part of the royal palace grounds located in the city center of The Hague in the Netherlands.

spots.name: Scheveningen Lighthouse
spots.summary: De Scheveningen Lighthouse is a lighthouse in Scheveningen, Netherlands. It was designed by Quirinus Harder and activated finished in 1875.

spots.name: Fotomuseum Den Haag

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Fotomuseum Den Haag is a photography museum in The Hague. The museum was founded in 2002. It was a spin-off of the nearby Kunstmuseum Den Haag, when then director Wim van Krimpen decided that the Kunstmuseum's collection of photography had become so rich that it deserved a separate location.

spots.name: Hofwijck
spots.summary: Hofwijck is a mansion built for 17th-century politician Constantijn Huygens. It is located in Voorburg on the Vliet canal from The Hague to Leiden. The formal address of the cultural heritage is 2 Westeinde, Voorburg, the Netherlands, but its location today is better known as the Voorburg railway station.

spots.name: Spuipoort
spots.summary: The Spuipoort was one of the gates which used to make it possible to leave the Binnenhof in Den Haag. The gate stood on an island. There was a fixed bridge between the island and the Binnenhof, and on the other side of the gate there was a drawbridge.

spots.name: Koninklijke Schouwburg
spots.summary: The Koninklijke Schouwburg is a theater in the city center of The Hague. The theater was built in 1766 and has been in use as theater since 1804. From 2017 it is one of the theaters in use by the national theater company Het Nationale Theater, but also other companies perform in the Schouwburg.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Mesdag Collection

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mesdag Collection is an art museum in The Hague, Netherlands. It is managed by the Van Gogh Museum.

spots.name: Stadhuis
spots.summary: In the early 1990s, the municipality moved to this enormous white building by American architect Richard Meier, nicknamed by locals as the Ice Palace. Walk in to have a look at the lofty main hall, which has exhibits on various topics related to the city. The two air bridges through the hall connecting the various offices had to be fenced off to prevent suicides, but still make for a nice view of

photo.author: Paul van de Velde from Netherlands

spots.name: Palace Gardens
spots.summary: This is the royal palace that King Willem-Alexander uses as his office. While the inside is not open to the public, the 17th-century façade can be seen from Noordeinde street, which also has a large number of art galleries. In the summer of 2023 the palace will be opened daily 10:00–17:00 to the public for the limited period of 1–13 August (7 August excepted). The {{marker

spots.name: Park Clingendael
spots.summary: A part of a former estate, the park is best known for its Japanese garden, one of the oldest (1910) in Europe. While the garden is open only a short period of time, the surrounding area is open all year long.

spots.name: Cafe Momfer de Mol

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cafe Momfer de Mol is located in the centre of the old Hague a place steeped in history. The cafe in its present form has been in existence since 2003, and is one of the finest laid-back cafe-bars of the city. The warm interiors and the informal ambiance at the cafe, are ideal allies to its delightful snack menu.

spots.name: Bodega de Posthoorn

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A grand cafe at the centre of The Hague, near tourist attractions such as Maurtishuis, Hofvijver, Binnenhof, Historical Museum and Escher Museum. It is a unique eating and drinking establishment with typical Dutch grandeur. You should at least have a cup of coffee here, to experience the grandeur.

spots.name: De Grote Markt

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Throughout the centuries the market square of The Hague has transformed into a grand outdoor café surrounded by bars and clubs. From early in the morning, until late at night you’ll find people having a good time here. In the summertime, the ‘Grote Markt’ is often home to musical events.

spots.name: Irodion

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Greek restaurant in the city centre. It is made up of two restaurants; the first one is fast food take out, where you can get the ubiquitous giros and tzatziki, with a generous portion of French fries. The second part is a fancier eat-in restaurant. Highly recommended.

spots.name: NOH
spots.summary: NOH is one of the most relaxing and finest Japanese sushi restaurants in The Hague, providing all the basics for an enjoyable evening. They regularly serve Toro and Uni and have a sushibar for single (travelling) people.

spots.name: Calla's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Modern and with painstaking preparation techniques. Shorter, concentration on cuisson, light sauces and rich in taste. Food at Calla's is in the classical French tradition stripped of all frills and furbelows.

spots.name: Bogor

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Known by the in-crowd as traditionally the best place in town. Simple but excellent food, has been around for over 40 years and has not changed.

spots.name: Kiraku

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Open since 1992. It's a small restaurant with a sushibar, the sushi taste excellent so make a reservation or come in early for dinner.

spots.name: Kaa Lun Palace

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Most 'local' Chinese people seem to come here. It has really good Chinese food, though the service is generally rated below average.

spots.name: Keraton Damai

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small 'living-room style restaurant' with very personal and attentive service. Small but excellent choice of dishes.

spots.name: 27 Club

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Named after artists who died 27 years old, among who Brian Jones, Kurt Cobain, Janis Joplin and Amy Winehouse.

spots.name: Dudok

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dudok lies right opposite the Binnenhof and is quite popular with politicians and the public out shopping.

spots.name: Palembang

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cosy place with excellent food. Lots of pictures on the wall with local celebrities who visited here.

spots.name: Fat Kee

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Preferred by Indian, Dutch and people from Suriname. Has a superb chicken and broccoli dish.

spots.name: Soeboer
spots.summary: Small restaurant, since 1958. Nasi Rames for €12.95 is an excellent menu for take out.

spots.summary: Also a venue for concerts and such. Prinsegracht 12.
